calls.body: At home, the Sharks keep sending Gaudette’s line (Goodrow, Ostapchuk and Gaudette) out against opponents’ fourth lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Ryan Warsofsky keeps choosing line for line. Tonight the Flames’ fourth line is Strömgren, Castagna and Suniev.

calls.head: Don’t buy Askarov’s record against the Flames
calls.body: Since 2023-24, Askarov has been a wall against the Flames, well above his usual. Fans love a pattern like this, but we checked three seasons of them and they predicted nothing. Don’t be surprised if the Flames finally get to him.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Castagna scores his first two NHL goals as the Flames beat the Sharks
paras: Adam Gaudette struck first for the Sharks early in the first, but Matt Coronato tied it 1-1 for Calgary a little over a minute later. Martin Pospíšil put the Flames ahead 2-1 with 38 seconds left in the period. Šimon Nemec scored his first goal for Calgary on the power play early in the second to make it 3-1. Jonathan Castagna, in his 19th NHL game, scored his first NHL goal, set up by Aydar Suniev, early in the third to make it 4-1. With the goalie pulled and less than five minutes left, Mason Marchment cut Calgary’s lead to 4-2 on the power play. Castagna scored his second NHL goal into the empty net with a minute left.

Don’t let the score fool you: the chances were a lot closer than that. Dustin Wolf made 21 saves for the Flames, and Yaroslav Askarov stopped 24 of 28 at the other end. Nobody on the ice had a bigger night than Yan Kuznetsov, by our Swing measure.
Zack Ostapchuk picked up a ten-minute misconduct. The Flames moved to 10-11-1 and climbed to fifth in the Pacific, while the Sharks fell to 10-12-2, fourth in the Pacific.

items.text: The Flames have beaten the Sharks four straight times, going back to last season.

The Flames have won both meetings this season.
